<div class="page-hero-inner">
<div class="eyebrow">Research</div>
<h1>Local institutions, public goods, and metropolitan growth.</h1>
<p>My research studies how the organization of local government changes incentives, coordination, fiscal capacity, and growth across U.S. metropolitan areas.</p>
</div>
</header>
<section class="content-band">
<p class="section-kicker">Job Market Paper</p>
<h2 class="section-title">Coordination vs. Competition</h2>
<p class="section-lede">The central question is whether growth is promoted by centralized governments concentrated in a few large units or decentralized governments made up of many smaller units.</p>
<div class="grid-two">
<article class="paper-card">
<div class="paper-topline">
<span class="tag coral">Job market paper</span>
<span class="tag">IV strategy</span>
<span class="tag gold">U.S. metropolitan areas</span>
</div>
<div class="paper-body">
<h2>Coordination vs. Competition: Local Government Centralization and Metropolitan Growth</h2>
<p class="abstract"><strong>Abstract.</strong> How does the organization of local government affect population growth? Is growth promoted in centralized governments concentrated in a few large units or decentralized governments consisting of many smaller units? The literature provides conflicting answers to these questions. On one hand, decentralization can promote competition between local governments, providing a market-like mechanism to obtain efficiency in the supply of public goods. On the other, externalities can foster coordination failures that undermine competition.</p>
<p class="abstract">In this paper, I use local government employment data from the metropolitan statistical areas of the United States and an IV strategy to estimate the causal effect of local government centralization on growth. I then examine the effect of centralization on local government employment, finances, and the siting decisions of data centers to determine which mechanisms drive the effect on growth.</p>
<p class="abstract">My instrument is derived from a complete history of post offices in the United States and leverages a historical policy change, the implementation of Rural Free Delivery in 1902, to measure the presence of small communities and dispersed populations. Using the variation induced by the instrument, I find that centralization causes higher population growth rates, higher total local government employment, more tax revenue to be collected, and fewer data centers to locate in the metropolitan area.</p>
<div class="paper-links">
<a href="WIEDEMANN_MUNI_CENTRALIZATION_2026.pdf">Download PDF</a>
<a href="../../index.html">Back to home</a>
</div>
</div>
</article>
<aside class="note-panel">
<h3>Paper details</h3>
<p><strong>Setting:</strong> U.S. metropolitan statistical areas.</p>
<p><strong>Instrument:</strong> historical post office patterns and Rural Free Delivery in 1902.</p>
<p><strong>Mechanisms:</strong> local government employment, finances, and data center location decisions.</p>
</aside>
</div>
</section>
<section class="content-band tint">
<p class="section-kicker">What The Paper Measures</p>
<h2 class="section-title">From institutional structure to economic outcomes.</h2>
<div class="grid-three">
<article class="feature-card">
<h3>Growth</h3>
<p>Population growth in U.S. metropolitan areas provides the main outcome for evaluating the net effect of local government centralization.</p>
</article>
<article class="feature-card">
<h3>Government Capacity</h3>
<p>Employment and revenue outcomes help evaluate whether centralization changes the scale and capacity of local public provision.</p>
</article>
<article class="feature-card">
<h3>Firm Location</h3>
<p>Data center siting decisions offer an additional mechanism for understanding how local structure shapes development.</p>
</article>
</div>
</section>
<section class="content-band">
<p class="section-kicker">Empirical Design</p>
<h2 class="section-title">A historical instrument for modern local government organization.</h2>
<div class="timeline">
<div class="timeline-item">
<div class="time">Historical source</div>
<div>
<h3>Post office history</h3>
<p>The instrument uses a complete history of U.S. post offices to measure the historical presence of small communities and dispersed populations.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="timeline-item">
<div class="time">Policy change</div>
<div>
<h3>Rural Free Delivery in 1902</h3>
<p>The design leverages the implementation of Rural Free Delivery as a historical shift that affected the organization of local communities.</p>
</div>
</div>
<div class="timeline-item">
<div class="time">Modern outcomes</div>
<div>
<h3>Metropolitan structure and growth</h3>
<p>The resulting variation shifts modern local government organization toward decentralization, allowing the paper to estimate causal effects on growth and related mechanisms.</p>
</div>
</div>
</div>
</section>
